land.text: that doab with 'dominion over lands to the south-east extending as far as the Hyphasis (Beas River)', 'the entire territory east of the Hydaspes', and 'the territories of Glausae, who ruled to the northeast' (Sialkot 60 km for Glausae; Gujranwala, Lahore and Amritsar for the lands toward the Beas); the Hydaspes page: 'Macedon annexes most of Punjab, from the Hydaspes to the Hyphasis', and from 321 'the territories along the Indus River' (the lower Indus band of Sindh and the Multan country)

successors.note: Porus 'reportedly died sometime between 321 and 315 BC' (the page); 'Eudemus, who had served as Alexander's satrap in the Punjab region, killed Porus' (infobox reign 'before 326 - c. 317 BC'). Eudemus and Taxiles left India in 316 (Indian-campaign page) and Chandragupta's Mauryas took the north-west after that (sa-02).

At Triparadisus (321) 'Antipater recognized Porus' authority over the territories along the Indus River'; the Peithon page has 'Lands on the river Indus, with the city Patala' going to Porus. region.text: 'Porus ruled over the tracts between the rivers Hydaspes (Jhelum) and Acesines (Chenab)': the doab around Gujrat and Sargodha

ledger.note: 326 BCE: Porus's kingdom between the Jhelum and the Chenab faces Alexander. 'Porus ruled over the tracts between the rivers Hydaspes (Jhelum) and Acesines (Chenab)'; infobox 'Reign: before 326 - c. 317 BC'. The page gives no year for the founding of the kingdom, so -326 is the first dated year and the confidence is 1.

region.text: the territories of Glausae, to the north-east of Porus's kingdom (Sialkot country)

ledger.note: 326 BCE: Porus's kingdom is restored and enlarged with the land of the Glausae, annexed by Alexander's forces. The page: Porus's territory 'was not only restored, but also expanded', 'with Alexander's forces annexing the territories of Glausaes, who ruled to the northeast of Porus' kingdom' (wording corrected by the reviewer, 2026-10-18: the annexation is Alexander's, the land goes to Porus). The page does not date the annexation; it follows the battle on the Hydaspes (May 326 BC on the Hydaspes page, July on the Indian-campaign page).

region.text: the lands south-east of Porus's doab toward the Hyphasis (Beas)

ledger.note: 326 BCE: Alexander extends Porus's land to the Hyphasis. 'Alexander not only reinstated him as his satrap but also expanded his jurisdiction' (Porus page), 'dominion over lands to the south-east extending as far as the Hyphasis'; 'Macedon annexes most of Punjab, from the Hydaspes to the Hyphasis' and 'left King Porus in charge of this easternmost territory' (Hydaspes page, May 326). The land had no state of its own on the pages.

region.text: the territories along the Indus River in Sindh and the Multan country, with Patala

ledger.note: 321 BCE: Antipater recognises Porus's authority along the Indus. 'After Perdiccas' murder in 321 BC, Antipater became the new regent. Antipater recognized Porus' authority over the territories along the Indus River.' The Peithon page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peithon_(son_of_Agenor)) has 'Lands on the river Indus, with the city Patala' going to Porus at Triparadisus. The Indus country had been Peithon's satrapy (hindush dossier).

wars.name: Battle of the Hydaspes
wars.outcome: Macedonian victory: 'Alexander spared Porus and made him a satrap'; Porus's land was extended to the Hyphasis ('Macedon annexes most of Punjab, from the Hydaspes to the Hyphasis').
wars.note: Infobox 'May 326 BC'; the Indian-campaign page has 'July 326 BC'. Taxila's ruler (Omphis, Ambhi) fought on Alexander's side; Abisares 'offered submission'.

certainty.note: A kingdom known from Alexander's historians; the pages give rivers and neighbours, not a frontier, and the late Indus grant is a single sentence on two pages.

notes: Porus rules as Alexander's satrap after 326, so the Macedonian Empire dossier (eu-02) should carry vassal_start (326) and vassal_end (317) for this slug; this dossier cannot add them. The shape is the union of named rivers and neighbours (Gujrat, Sargodha, Sialkot, Gujranwala, Lahore, Amritsar): none of these is a boundary on the pages. The start is the first dated year (the page says 'before 326' and gives no earlier event). The Indus grant of 321 rests on two summaries (the Porus page and the Peithon page) that name 'the territories along the Indus River' and 'Patala'; its extent is my reading of the lower Indus, and it is the land of the hindush dossier (Sindh and Multan), which ended in -325, so the two do not overlap in time. The page contradicts itself on Porus's death (c. 317 in the infobox; between 321 and 315 in the text). Taxila (Ambhi/Omphis, Taxiles) and Abisares (Kashmir and the Hazara country) were Porus's neighbours and Alexander's other client kings; neither has a dossier (see counterparts). The Hydaspes page says May, the Indian-campaign page July, for the battle. Gazetteer: none missing.
